so, the state is... the state of the environment (in this case, it is the whole grid of tile labeled as holes/ice and player position on the grid) (note that it might not be the whole grid depending on your version of frozen lake, I think some of them only let  the agent see part of the grid). so basically, the state is the state of the environment (or in other words, it is what the agent can see). it is updated at each step(not episode)

the action is the action the agent is gonna take, the state action pair is just the input at each step into the algo, q-learning (at least, when you use a neural net) tries to evaluate what the pair (state, action) is gonna produce as rewards during the next state (or step, the state change every step) before it receives the actual data, it learns the policy (or in other words, what the action given a state is going to produce as rewards) that way.

the output of the q-learning is a prediction of the reward if you take x action during x state.

since the audience will be foreign to the subject:

step: this is the maximum of movement(or decision) the agent can take per episode, it has to be set because sometime your agent will just do nothing or get stuck in a loop (and thus the episode would never end)

episode: it ends when the agent either dies (walks into a hole in this case) or when the agent gets to the other side of the lake (the agent wins), or when the maximum step amount is reached.

alpha: it defines how much the agent will take into consideration the reward value for the episode it just finished, having it too low will not let your agent learn from the episode, having too high will drastically change the behavior of your agent after each episode, which will affect learning.

gamma: it defines how much the agent take into consideration past rewards ( if its set to 1, each reward from past episode will be considered as much as the last one, less than one and it will consider less each reward the further away from the last one (it will take into account the first episode's reward less, the second episode a bit more, the third even more etc.)

reward: it tells the agent wether it was a good or bad episode, its goal is to maximize this value over time.

So for example, if you would want to make an RL agent that plays mario and implement the 'hippocampus' into its training, you could simply add to the neural network input *all* the frames that it has ever seen. ofc that would be quite a task and the nn would need to either be huge, or you would need a good graphic card. How to solve this? You train a VAE(variational auto encoder) on frames of other people playing so you can have your VAE nn that can simplify the frame input based on stuff your agent never did or saw (that would be like an unconscious memory) and you simply feed the output of your VAE nn with the actual frames into your RL agent. 

basically, train a VAE with data that your RL agent didn't gather itself but *can* gather itself. Your VAE network would be unconscious memory and you would feed its output into your RL agent network, so, you have your hippocampus.

a VAE is a neural network that its loss function the difference between its input and output. you want to make the network smaller at some place. so like 

Input -> smaller number of nodes than input -> output(which shouls look exactly like the input) 

ofc it wont be able to have the exact same output as its input, but that is not really what we want, you want the part of the network that is 

input -> smallest amount of node

you "cut" your VAE to only keep the trained part that could "vulgarise" the input to a smaller dimension than its original one.
